findings.evidence: "For the working method, begin at Ch. 1 (The Token) and follow the canonical workload through Chs. 16–17 and 20–21"
findings.issue: Referent defect: "Ch. 1 (The Token)" conflates Chapter 1 with Part I. Chapter 1 is titled "It All Starts With the First Token"; "The Token" is the Part I divider title. A reader following this instruction may look for a chapter titled "The Token".
findings.fix_instruction: Change to "begin at Ch. 1 ('It All Starts With the First Token', Part I)" or "begin with Part I (The Token), starting at Ch. 1".

findings.evidence: "A section reference takes the form § N.M, which means Chapter N, Section M — so § 1.4 is Ch. 1, Section 4 (Measurement), not Section 1's fourth subsection."
findings.issue: Convention inconsistency: the Preface defines the form as "§ N.M" (with a space), but the body predominantly uses the no-space form ("§7.3", "§4.6", "§8.3.3", "§6.3.4") and occasionally the spaced form ("§ 7.3", "§ 1.4"). Both forms are in use across the book, so the stated convention does not match the actual style.
findings.fix_instruction: Pick one form (recommend the no-space "§N.M" used by the majority of the body) and either normalize the whole book or state that the space is optional.

findings.evidence: "read any 'meets 1.2 s' statement as conditional on a named tested workload and end-to-end timing (S-01)"
findings.issue: S-01 is referenced as a parenthetical shorthand but is never defined or introduced anywhere in the Preface or preceding chapters visible in the document. A reader encountering it here has no way to resolve the reference without reaching Chapter 14 (benchmarking protocol) approximately 240 pages later, and there is no forward-pointing explanation (e.g., 'S-01, defined in Ch. 14').
findings.fix_instruction: Either define S-01 at first use with a brief parenthetical (e.g., '(S-01, the Chapter 14 benchmark scenario)'), or add an explicit forward pointer such as '(S-01; defined in Ch. 14 § 1).'

findings.evidence: Page 16: "The four terms below are the ones a reader meets most often; each names its axis, and each is the same item as the matching value defined further down this section." The four terms are MEASURED, ANALYTICAL, ILLUSTRATIVE, HYPOTHESIS. Page 17 then defines the full Axis 3 list: "measurement status therefore uses ANALYTICAL, SCENARIO-DERIVED, MODELED, MEASURED or UNMEASURED" — five values, and the epistemic-status list (FACT, DERIVED, ASSUMPTION, HYPOTHESIS, UNRESOLVED) contains five more.
findings.issue: The Preface presents 'four terms' as 'the ones a reader meets most often' but the actual Axis 3 measurement-status enumeration has five values (ANALYTICAL, SCENARIO-DERIVED, MODELED, MEASURED, UNMEASURED), and the book in fact uses SCENARIO-DERIVED (p. 94: "SCENARIO-DERIVED is the Axis-3 stage a canonical-scenario value normally reports"), MODELED, and UNMEASURED in the body. A reader looking for the full label set in the Preface's summary panel finds four terms where the chapter's own axis definition has five, and the page never says which three Axis-3 values are 'less common'. The panel also warns 'The four terms above are not four parallel registers' — but 'register' here is a fifth, undefined term (the book otherwise uses 'axis'), and 'register' is never defined in the Sources chapter either.
findings.fix_instruction: Replace 'The four terms below are the ones a reader meets most often' with an explicit enumeration of the five Axis-3 measurement statuses (or state which are omitted and why), and replace the undefined word 'register' with 'axis' throughout the evidence-discipline panel so the panel uses only terms the Sources chapter defines.

findings.evidence: Page 19: "Prefill latency is not interchangeable with TTFT: prefill is a component of, not identical to, the user-observed TTFT. In the book's convention (Ch. 2, 4), TTFTe2e = retrieval + admission/queue + tokenization/transfer + prefill". Page 36 (Ch. 2 §2.1) repeats: "TTFTe2e = retrieval + admission/queue + tokenization/transfer + prefill". Page 90 (Ch. 4 Table 4-1) repeats the same form. Page 42 (Ch. 2 §2.3): "TTFT budget 1.2 s (retrieval ~120 ms + prefill)" — the two-term form. Page 79 (Ch. 4 §4.3 'Latency from SLO'): "TTFT (time-to-first-token): budget of 1.2 s, comprising retrieval (~120 ms for vector search and reranking on a local GPU) + prefill (budget cap 1.08 s for 9,200 tokens across the 8×H100 canonical host)".
findings.issue: The book states a four-term TTFT convention (retrieval + admission/queue + tokenization/transfer + prefill) but then, in Ch. 2 §2.3 (p. 42) and Ch. 4 §4.3 (p. 79), restates the budget as the two-term form 'retrieval ~120 ms + prefill' with the 1.2 s total, without flagging on those two statements that admission/queue and tokenization/transfer are excluded. The qualifier exists only in the Preface (p. 19), Table 4-2 (p. 94: 'budget_prefill ≤ 1.08 s − B_other'), and the Ch. 4 canonical box. A reader who lands on Ch. 2 §2.3 or Ch. 4 §4.3 — the two places the budget is actually used — reads '1.2 s = retrieval + prefill' as the operative definition, contradicting the book's own stated convention two pages earlier.
findings.fix_instruction: At every restatement of the 1.2 s TTFT budget (Ch. 2 §2.3, Ch. 4 §4.3 and its Table 4-1 latency row), carry the same four-term convention or an inline parenthetical 'admission/queue + tokenization/transfer not yet budgeted — see Preface TTFT convention', so the two-term shorthand is never presented as the definition.

findings.evidence: Page 16: "A claim carries the labels directly (inline) or via an identified table or section that states them (e.g. a worked-example table whose header or footnote gives provenance and status for every row)". Page 17: "purely illustrative or rhetorical numbers that no later calculation depends on may carry them in the surrounding prose — exceptions are defined unambiguously in the Sources, Method, and Reproducibility chapter."
findings.issue: The Preface delegates the definition of its own label exceptions to the Sources, Method, and Reproducibility chapter (p. 508), and asserts those exceptions are 'defined unambiguously' there. The Prefuse's own panel therefore cannot be audited without the later chapter, and the cross-reference from a normative evidence rule to a chapter 480 pages later is a single point of failure: if the Sources chapter's wording differs, there is no mechanism for the Preface to stay in sync. The Preface also says 'The full label rule set lives in the Sources, Method, and Reproducibility chapter' (p. 16) while simultaneously presenting a nearly complete rule set inline — two sources of truth for one rule set.
findings.fix_instruction: Either move the complete label rule set into the Preface (with a short pointer to the Sources chapter for the verification procedure only), or state in the Preface which specific numbered subsection of the Sources chapter holds the exceptions and add a normative 'if these conflict, this page governs' line.

findings.evidence: Page 20 ends the Preface: 'The Appendix therefore surveys the frontier open-weight architectures of 2026, mapped back to the mechanisms and decisions explored in the body of the book — and closes on the question that is more durable than any single architecture: where should the intelligence live.' Page 21 is the Part I divider.
findings.issue: The Preface's final paragraph tells the reader what Appendix A does ('surveys the frontier open-weight architectures of 2026 ... closes on the question ... where should the intelligence live'), and the Contents (p. 7) confirms 'Appendix A — 2026 Frontier Architecture Signals: Four Open-Weight Model Families . . . 467'. But the front matter contains no List of Figures for Appendix A's figures either — the List of Figures does include 'A.1 ... A.5' (pp. 10), so Appendix A's figure list is present. The defect is in the Contents (p. 7): the Appendix A entry names 'Four Open-Weight Model Families' while the List of Figures (p. 10) names five appendix figures including 'A.3 A chronology of frontier AI systems, ~2017 to ~2026' and 'A.4 Where should intelligence live? The horizontal bands are a design choice' — the latter matching the Preface's closing question. The Appendix's own subsections are referenced throughout the body as '§9A', '§A.7', '§A.3', '§A.10', 'Appendix A §9A' — a numbering scheme ('9A') that the front matter never lists, so no reader can resolve '§9A' or '§A.7' or '§A.10' from the front matter.
findings.fix_instruction: Add an appendix subsection list (A.1–A.10) to the front matter Contents, with page numbers, so the body's §9A / §A.3 / §A.7 / §A.10 pointers resolve; and reconcile the Appendix A title with the number of families actually surveyed.

findings.evidence: Page 16: "ILLUSTRATIVE (Axis 1, provenance) — a non-canonical worked example ([ILLUSTRATIVE], paired with ASSUMPTION or DERIVED), chosen to make a calculation concrete and re-derived per deployment; this is a provenance tag only, not a measurement status (see the Axis note below). [canonical scenario] and [ILLUSTRATIVE] are distinct Axis-1 provenances: the canonical scenario is the book's fixed reference set, computed on its teaching geometry (Ch. 4, Table 4-2), and ILLUSTRATIVE covers non-canonical examples only — teaching geometry belongs to the canonical scenario, and it does not define ILLUSTRATIVE."
findings.issue: The Preface says ILLUSTRATIVE must be 'paired with ASSUMPTION or DERIVED'. But Ch. 1 (p. 29, p. 30) uses '[ILLUSTRATIVE][ASSUMPTION] conceptual' and '[ILLUSTRATIVE][DERIVED]' for figures; Ch. 6 (p. 111) uses '[ILLUSTRATIVE conceptual]' with no Axis-2 partner; Ch. 6 (p. 134) uses '[ILLUSTRATIVE synthetic profile]' with no Axis-2 partner; Ch. 7 (p. 156) uses '[ILLUSTRATIVE][DERIVED]' and (p. 161) '[ILLUSTRATIVE][DERIVED]'; Ch. 8 (p. 187 area) uses '[ILLUSTRATIVE conceptual, roofline developed in Ch 8]'. So 'conceptual' and 'synthetic profile' are used as Axis-2 partners in place of the two permitted values, in at least four places — a systematic label-form violation against the book's own declared rule.
findings.fix_instruction: Either permit 'conceptual'/'synthetic' as a declared third Axis-2 value for figures and say so in the Preface, or replace every '[ILLUSTRATIVE conceptual]' and '[ILLUSTRATIVE synthetic profile]' with '[ILLUSTRATIVE][DERIVED]' (or the appropriate Axis-2 tag) so all ILLUSTRATIVE tags pair with ASSUMPTION or DERIVED as the Preface requires.

findings.evidence: Page 19: "Terminology. GPU memory and VRAM are used generically for accelerator-local memory; HBM means high-bandwidth-memory specifically, which is what the worked examples assume." Page 43 (Ch. 2): "140 GB in aggregate, or a 17.5 GB shard per GPU on the canonical 8×H100 host at TP = 8". Page 124 (Ch. 7): "HBM means high-bandwidth-memory specifically".
findings.issue: The terminology convention is declared for GPU memory/VRAM vs HBM, but the book repeatedly uses 'GPU memory', 'VRAM' and 'HBM' interchangeably for the same quantity within single sentences — e.g. p. 106: 'A 70B FP16 model (140 GB weights) fits on a single host with 8×H100 (640 GB GPU memory)' and '640 GB pool' and 'the ~436 GB KV budget' (a budget that is a GPU-memory quantity); p. 148 Table 7-1: '2×H100 total VRAM | 2 ×80 GB = 160 GB' and '8×H100 total VRAM | 640 GB' while the same chapter elsewhere calls the 640 GB pool 'HBM' (p. 146: 'the canonical 8×H100 pool reads 640 GB'). The declared convention ('HBM means high-bandwidth-memory specifically, which is what the worked examples assume') implies the worked examples say HBM, but the worked examples mostly say 'GPU memory' or 'VRAM' and only occasionally HBM.
findings.fix_instruction: Either change the convention to state that GPU memory / VRAM / HBM are used interchangeably for accelerator-local memory in the worked examples (with HBM used only where the bandwidth or technology is the point), or normalize the worked examples to 'HBM' as the declared convention requires.

findings.evidence: Page 18: "Evidence cutoff and edition date. This edition is build v20260913 (2026-09-13) with a single evidence cutoff of 2026-08-30 ... Post-cutoff policy: any model, price or spec that changed after 2026-08-30 is not silently updated in this edition; a later build revalidates the fast-moving claims against current vendor documentation and flags any post-cutoff change separately rather than inheriting the prior value." Page 18 also: "Dated addenda sit outside that snapshot. Appendix A, A.6 carries a boxed 2026-09-27 capability probe under revision v20260913+addendum-20260927; the separately dated 2026-10-28 technology notes in the body and Appendix A carry revision v20260913+addendum-20261028; and a superseding re-verification of the DeepSeek model-service status (Appendix A, A.3) is recorded under v20260913+addendum-20261101".
findings.issue: Three addendum revisions are declared (20260927, 20261028, 20261101) and the Preface states they 'distinguish inspected sources and code from locally reproduced measurements; neither addendum silently updates the original August comparisons or the First-hand Sources list.' However, the Ch. 7 §7.3.1 Intel Arc Pro inspection (p. 152), the Ch. 8 §8.1.1 and §8.1.3 backend observations (pp. 175, 177), the Ch. 5 footnotes 1–4 (pp. 113, 124) and the Ch. 3 §3.6.2 Wan2.2 inspection (p. 68) are all dated 2026-10-28 material inside the body — the Preface says they 'carry revision v20260913+addendum-20261028', but no addendum revision marker appears at any of those body locations (only the prose dates). A reader auditing which claims fall under which addendum revision has to reconstruct it from dates.
findings.fix_instruction: Print the addendum revision identifier (v20260913+addendum-20261028) alongside the date at each body location that falls under it — Ch. 5 footnotes 1–4, Ch. 3 §3.6.2, Ch. 7 §7.3.1, Ch. 8 §8.1.1, §8.1.3 and the Ch. 2 §2.1.2 note — so the Preface's addenda registry is verifiable from the pages themselves.

findings.evidence: The canonical model is a constructed full-MHA teaching geometry (80 layers, hidden size 8192), not a named vendor checkpoint; Ch. 4's 'CANONICAL TEACHING MODEL' callout states the intent: GQA/MQA and sparse attention shrink the KV constant several-fold in 2026 production models, so the book's ∼2.62 MB/token is a deliberate upper bound.
findings.issue: KV per token 2.62 MB/token stated as upper bound but arithmetic not shown until Ch 7 - early readers may apply as universal constant contradicting Ch 7 GQA calculation where KV ~0.33 MB/token for Llama-2/3 70B.
findings.fix_instruction: Add inline derivation on page 12: 2*80*8192*2 bytes = 2,621,440 bytes = 2.62 MB/token at FP16, and note GQA reduces by factor n_kv_heads/n_heads.
